content:
Rae: heads-up: after yesterday's int8 compact rollout to canary, we've got a small perf/quality regression on long-context chat tests — memory looks better but some recall/consistency drops. Posting quick traces.

Diego: can you paste the perf traces? KV pager behavior suspected.

Rae: here's a short profiler dump from the failing test run:
```
perf.summary: 
kv_hit_rate: 0.86
kv_spill_rate: 0.19
kv_dequant_cycles: 0.042
longctx_top1_drift: 0.007
```

Anya: interesting — spill_rate jumped after we enabled the "elastic-compact" compaction in the INT8 path? that was meant to save ~25% memory.

Samir: do we have kernel selection changes with that build? I remember kernel-pin fallback touching batching heuristics.

Rae: yes — kernel pinning was enabled (PR #4897). also the stride-batcher got a tweak so it batches fewer tokens for longctx to avoid latency SLOs.

Diego: fewer tokens batched -> less KV reuse across contiguous requests -> more reads -> read-amplification. that could amplify small quant noise into measurable logits drift.

Anya: is the accuracy drop localized to certain prompt types or appears across the board? any eval diffs?

Rae: localized to long-history QA and multi-turn summarization. eval shows top-1 drift on 8k prompts: ~0.7 BLEU-like pts. traces show more frequent page churn + dequant/rehydrate for int8 pages.

Samir: plausible cause: int8 pages when evicted then rehydrated hit dequant path which is noisy. plus compaction can create fragmentation that increases eviction frequency. we should try compaction=lazy or pin hot pages.

Diego: agreed. quick experiment: toggle compaction to lazy and force BF16 kernel for a canary. anyone available to roll?

Anya: i can run a canary patch on staging. will test both compaction modes + kernel variants. samir — can you add a temporary dashboard widget for page-churn vs BLEU?

Samir: on it. adding kv.page_churn, kv.dequant_cycles, and a hotness heatmap. also tracking kv.page_pin_hits.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for canary-precision-expt-2026-03-18 (sha: a1b2c3).

Rae: also note the stride-batcher change likely shortens KV lifetime per request group — tuning batch TTL may be faster than disabling compaction.

Diego: we should update kernel ranking: current cost func rewards int8 for latency but ignores dequant penalty. add a 'rehydrate_penalty' to ranking.

Anya: good call. i'll add a small +0.05 penalty for kernels with high dequant counts in ranking heuristics.

Samir: running the two-experiment suite now (lazy-compaction+BF16 vs elastic-compact+int8 with kernel-penalty). ETA ~45m.

Rae: if reproduced, short-term plan = rollback int8 compaction in prod. medium-term = kernel ranking change + adaptive pinning for top hot pages. I'll draft an RFC after the canary.

Diego: also capture kv.page_pin_hits vs kv.page_evicts so we can tune adaptive pin threshold; if pin memory cost too high we fallback to partial-pin for top-5% hottest pages.

deploy-bot: canary completed: compaction=lazy + BF16 kernel reduced page_churn by 62%, BLEU recovered ~0.5 pts (partial). full regression suite still running.

Rae: great. next steps: rollback plan for prod int8 compaction, bake dequant penalty into kernel selection, and tune batch TTL. i'll open follow-ups.

Diego: thanks all — ping when the full suite finishes.
